value: A D name may not suit international rules, and the table lets an alternate proper shipping name be chosen whether transport is domestic or international.
reason: Old explanation limited the alternate name to international transport. 172.101(b)(3) (p. 3): 'An alternate proper shipping name may be selected when either domestic or international transportation is involved.'

value: Cartons of paint prepared as limited quantities, containing no hazardous substance or waste, go by a for-hire trucking company. What must each carton show?
reason: 'By truck' also covers private motor carriage, where 172.315(a)(3) (p. 249) lets some small PG II and III loads go without the mark: 'for highway transportation by private motor carrier, the limited quantity marking is not required to be displayed'.

value: A for-hire carrier gets no private carrier exception, so the mark is required, and it replaces the § 172.301 marking when no hazardous substance or waste is inside.
reason: Goes with the front fix. 172.315(a) (p. 248): 'A package displaying this mark is not subject to the marking requirements of § 172.301'; 172.315(a)(3) (p. 249) exception is for 'private motor carrier' only.

value: Under § 173.133, what is a Division 6.1 liquid that meets the Packing Group I, Hazard Zone A or B criteria for vapour inhalation?
reason: 'What is it?' can be answered 'a poison' or 'PG I'; the card wants the PIH status. 173.133(a)(2) note 2 (p. 117): 'is a material poisonous by inhalation subject to the additional hazard communication requirements'.

value: LC50 is the concentration in air that kills half of the test animals, so the lower the LC50, the more toxic the material and the nearer it is to Zone A.
reason: 'How little ... it takes to be lethal to test animals' misstates LC50. 173.132(b)(3) (p. 115): LC50 'causes death within 14 days in half of the animals tested'; 173.116(a) (p. 106): Zone A is 'LC50 less than or equal to 200 ppm'.

value: Zone A is the most toxic band, so it has the lowest limit; Zones B, C and D have upper limits of 1000, 3000 and 5000 ppm.
reason: 'Follow at 1000, 3000 and 5000 ppm' reads as starting points; these are upper limits. 173.116(a) table (p. 106): B 'greater than 200 ppm and less than or equal to 1000 ppm'; C '... 3000 ppm'; D '... 5000 ppm'.

value: B: Zone B starts above 200 ppm. C: Zone D covers LC50 values above 3000 ppm, up to 5000 ppm. D: Division 2.3 gases are assigned hazard zones; only Divisions 2.1 and 2.2 have none.
reason: Zone D band given without its upper limit. 173.116(a) table (p. 106): D 'LC50 greater than 3000 ppm or less than or equal to 5000 ppm'.

value: The mark tells carriers the package holds a limited quantity; § 172.315(a)(3) spares only a few small private motor carrier loads, and the 'Y' mark is an allowed alternative.
reason: Back reads as if no other exception exists. 172.315(a) (p. 248): 'As an alternative, a packaging may display the limited quantity ‘‘Y’’ mark'; 172.315(a)(3) (p. 249): private motor carrier exception for PG II and III.

value: Under the 1 October 2025 text, what size must the limited quantity mark be?
reason: Since 3 September 2026 a 25 mm mark on the shipping label is also allowed (91 FR 49332, 172.315(a)(2)(iii): 'Each marking must be a minimum of 25 mm on each side'), so the unqualified question no longer has one answer.

value: A: Class 8 materials are assigned packing groups, so PG I must be shown. B: Class 3 materials are assigned packing groups, so PG II must be shown. C: Division 6.1 materials are assigned packing groups, so PG III must be shown.
reason: 'B, C and A:' is out of order and lumps three options together. 172.202(a)(4) (p. 234): 'The packing group in Roman numerals, as designated for the hazardous material in Column (5)'.

value: Section 172.604(a) puts this duty on the person who offers the material for transportation.
reason: 'Not on the carrier' is an inference the section does not state. 172.604(a) (p. 302): 'A person who offers a hazardous material for transportation must provide a numeric emergency response telephone number'.
